_readme: Proof the game is actually audible - through the real loop, the real input map and the
real map data, which no unit test can answer.
Every assertion is on the id that was REQUESTED. This runs headless on a dummy audio
driver, so 'a sound came out of the speakers' is not a claim any gate here can make;
'the world asked for a footstep when the player walked' is.
A new script rather than steps added to an existing one: Qa runs exactly one step per
physics frame, so inserting anything into a script shifts every later frame by one - and
fall_at_the_keep presses blind into a cue countdown and then asserts hp and level.

steps.text: the title opens the game now. A --qa-script run points saves at user://qa_saves and empties it at boot, so there is never anything to Continue - and the cursor opens on the row a press will actually do something with, which is New game. Rows: Continue, New game. One press starts the run.
the title has a theme, and it is asked for before a key is pressed - which is why this is asserted here rather than after the run starts
the opening line is forced, so dismiss it first
the voice can actually play what it names - the assertion that only bites against a packed build
talking to the warden asks for the page and the blip
the press that OPENS a dialog belongs to the world, not to the box - so the page turn is the NEXT one
